question: An investigator is studying the metabolism of an experimental drug that is known to have first order kinetics. Immediately after administering an intravenous dose of the drug to a patient, the serum concentration is 60 U/L. 3 hours later, the serum concentration of the drug is 30 U/L. 9 hours after administration, the serum concentration of the drug is most likely to be which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "First-order kinetics" -> "Drug concentration decreases exponentially over time" -> "Serum concentration at 9 hours will be lower than at 3 hours" -> "Serum concentration at 9 hours will be less than 30 U/L" -> "Most likely to be 15 U/L" -> 90%
analysis: Based on first-order kinetics, the drug concentration decreases exponentially over time. The half-life of the drug can be calculated using the formula t1/2 = 0.693/k, where k is the elimination rate constant. Given the initial concentration of 60 U/L and the concentration of 30 U/L at 3 hours, we can calculate the elimination rate constant (k) and then predict the concentration at 9 hours.
